narrative: Material PL1__MB3E07ED exhibits high-volume erratic daily demand (mean 8,118 units/day, CV 0.31) with a heavy-tailed distribution driven by periodic demand spikes. Lead times are highly unstable (CV 0.66, mean 1.52 days), with supply-side variability being the dominant buffer driver. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with reorder point 34,707 and order quantity 24,248 is recommended; this consolidates ~685 annual orders into ~84, saving $21,523/year (61.8%) while meeting the 95% service level with a safety stock of 14,251 units — far above the current SAP setting of 187.
warnings: CRITICAL: Recommended safety stock (14251 units) is 76.2x higher than current SAP setting (187 units). This indicates significant underestimation of demand/lead time variability.
RISK: Lead time variability is very high (CV=0.66). Consider supplier diversification or buffer stock positioning.
PATTERN: Demand classified as ERRATIC (high variability, regular occurrence). Consider demand smoothing initiatives or collaborative planning with customers.
DATA: 15 outliers detected (11.3% of data). Review for data quality issues or exceptional events.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand occurs every working day (non-zero fraction = 100%) with moderate-to-high CV (0.31), making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. EOQ sets the optimal batch size while the reorder point absorbs demand and lead-time uncertainty. A periodic review would be less responsive given the unstable lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap (90,078 units) does not bind: safety stock (14,251) + order quantity (24,248) = 38,499 units, well within capacity. No capacity-driven service degradation.
research_insights.escalation_flag: ESCALATE: Current SAP safety stock (187 units) is critically insufficient — 76x below the statistically required level. Immediate SAP parameter update required to avoid stockouts and service failures at the 95% target.
